review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.

build.evidence:
npm run build (turbo): 12 tasks successful, 0 failures. STATED PLAINLY AGAIN, as the previous recording of this gate did: apps/desktop is not an npm workspace, so none of this round's changes are build inputs and most of those tasks are cache hits. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous, and the evidence that matters is below.

WHAT THIS ROUND ADDRESSED, AND WHICH OF gpt-architect's NINE BULLETS IT IS. The round-111 verdict's last bullet: "strict notice generation fails on missing evidence rather than silently producing a green result". IT DID NOT, AND THAT IS NOW FIXED AND PROVEN.

THE DEFECT, EXACTLY. `collect-notices.mjs` walks `<sidecar>/server/node_modules`. If that directory was missing, empty, or laid out somewhere the walk does not read, `collect()` returned zero entries, `renderNotices` produced a document listing nothing, the script wrote it, printed "0 package(s), 0 with no licence evidence" and EXITED 0. `--strict` could not catch it: it fires on `attention.length > 0`, and a tree with no packages has nothing to attend to. So the strictest available setting was GREEN on the one input where the evidence was entirely absent -- an installer built on it would have shipped a confident, empty attribution claim.

That is the third instance of one shape in this project: `drizzle-kit migrate` applying nothing and exiting 0 (PL-0714, and again when PL-0726 found the hand-written replacement had grown its own version), and three e2e titles skipped in every configuration with no gate asking (PL-0717). Each reported success over an empty set.

THE FIX, IN TWO PLACES ON PURPOSE. `collect-notices.mjs` refuses a tree it found no packages in, and reads its own output back to confirm a non-empty file exists. `package-sidecar.mjs` then asserts the file is in the tree it is about to hand the bundler -- the same fact from the other side, because one asks "did I write it" and the other asks "is it in what ships", and a step inserted between them that cleaned the directory would leave the first passing.

PROVEN AGAINST REAL TREES, not described. Five cases, driving the actual script as a child process:
  A. a real-layout tree with two packages          -> exit 0, "2 package(s), 1 with no licence evidence", 1618-byte document
  B. --strict on it, one package lacking evidence  -> exit 1, the original behaviour, unchanged
  C. server/ present, node_modules absent          -> exit 1, "found no packages", AND NO DOCUMENT WRITTEN
  D. server/node_modules present and empty         -> exit 1
  E. --strict on the empty tree                    -> exit 1. This is the regression that mattered: it was 0 before.

AND THE TESTS WERE PROVEN NON-VACUOUS BY REMOVING THE FIX. With the empty-tree refusal deleted from collect-notices.mjs, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` goes 22 tests / 19 pass / 3 FAIL, naming exactly the three new refusals. Restored, 22/22, and `git diff --stat` confirms the file is the fixed one. A control case is in the suite too -- a tree that HAS packages still being described -- because a script that refused everything would satisfy every refusal assertion.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, AND IS NOT CLAIMED. Eight of the verdict's nine bullets are about THE CONTENTS OF A REAL WINDOWS PACKAGE TREE, and no such tree exists to inspect: Windows #14's `package` job failed, and Windows #15's (run 37210126408) was still IN PROGRESS when this was recorded. Specifically unproven: whether a libmpv/FFmpeg artifact is included at all and its provenance, version pin and configure flags; whether GPL-only components are excluded; whether THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is actually present in the installed tree; whether the Node LICENSE is beside the shipped runtime; and whether the collected dependency list reflects what was really packaged. The mechanism for every one of those exists and is now harder to fool, which is not the same as having looked.

TWO MECHANISM GAPS FOUND WHILE LOOKING, NEITHER FIXABLE FROM THIS SURFACE (apps/desktop/** and docs/LICENSING.md):
  - `scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs` requires four paths of the INSTALLED tree and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is not among them. The one check that inspects a real installation does not ask for the file the attribution obligation depends on.
  - `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` -- now 22 cases, including these five -- is still run by nothing automatically. apps/desktop is not a workspace and `npm run test:scripts` is in the root package.json. The same gap PL-0714 closed for two other suites.
Both are filed rather than reached into.

THE PATENT BOUNDARY IS UNTOUCHED, as the verdict requires: nothing here enables, assumes or infers anything about H.264/HEVC, and no decoder was added, configured or claimed.

review.title: Updates, and a version the application can prove
review.acceptance: The application can tell a user what version it is and can update itself safely, or states plainly that it cannot yet and why. REQUIRED: an update mechanism whose payloads are signature-verified -- an updater that fetches and executes an unverified binary is a remote code execution feature, and SECURITY.md's threat list already ranks unauthorized access above convenience. REQUIRED: the update endpoint is pinned and allowlisted like every other egress in this repository. REQUIRED: a rollback story, or a stated decision that there is none and what a user does instead. REQUIRED: the version is derived from one source shared with PW-0501. IF SIGNING IS UNAVAILABLE the update path must be disabled by default and say so, rather than shipping an unverified one -- an unsigned auto-updater is worse than no updater, and that dependency goes to LAST_MILE rather than being worked around.

build.evidence:
THE EXECUTABLE CLAUSES ARE DONE AND THE SIGNING-DEPENDENT ONES ARE STATED, which is what the acceptance conditional asks for: "IF SIGNING IS UNAVAILABLE the update path must be disabled by default and say so, rather than shipping an unverified one". Signing is unavailable (LAST_MILE 6), so that branch of the acceptance is the one in force and it is satisfied, not deferred.

THE DEFECT THIS FOUND, MEASURED. The repository has TWO independent version sources and nothing reconciled them. apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml [package] version is what Tauri names the installer from -- confirmed against reality, not inferred: Windows #16 and #17 both produced Project Liberty_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi, and tauri.conf.json declares no version so Tauri fell back to Cargo. apps/web/package.json version is what the About screen SHOWS A USER (PW-0308 renders it; settings.test.tsx asserts it is read, not pasted). Both read 0.1.0 today by coincidence of nobody having bumped either. The day one moves and the other does not, the About screen names a build that is not the build installed, and every defect report from it cites the wrong version -- while PW-0603 run sheet asks the commander for exactly that number and PW-0501 inventory identifies the build by the installer filename.

WHAT LANDED. checkVersionAuthority in scripts/validate-repo.mjs: the two must agree; tauri.conf.json must not carry a THIRD value, because Tauri uses it when present and falls back when absent, so a value there does not disagree with Cargo, it silently OVERRIDES it; and no updater may be configured while no signing key exists. It runs in CI validate job BEFORE npm ci and in repo:validate locally, so a half-done bump is caught on the machine that made it. No package.json or workflow edit was needed, which matters because both are reserved by tasks in review.

PROVEN BY DRIVING EACH REFUSAL AGAINST THE REAL REPOSITORY, then reverting: bumping apps/web alone to 0.2.0 fails naming both numbers; adding version 9.9.9 to tauri.conf.json fails naming the override; adding a plugins.updater fails naming the remote-code-execution path. Tree restored clean each time, confirmed by git diff --stat.

SUITE AND MUTATION. scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs gains 9 cases and reports 29 assertion groups passing; the whole file including its siblings is green (27 + 21 + 29). Mutation-tested per refusal: disabling the version-disagreement branch reddens 2 cases, disabling the updater branch reddens 1. Both mutants reverted and 29 re-run green. One case exists only to prove the [package] anchoring -- a pattern that merely looked for version = "..." would match the serde dependency line present in every Cargo.toml, compare serde version to the web app, fail on a correct repository and be deleted within a day.

cargo check on the desktop crate: exit 0, so the tauri.conf.json edits did not break the build.

docs/RELEASE.md states the boundary part by part -- version authority DONE, installed-version evidence DONE, update discovery NONE, download NONE, signature verification IMPOSSIBLE TODAY, application NONE, rollback NONE -- with the four things that must all exist before an updater can be built honestly, and the note that the first of them is not an engineering task. The rollback section states the real alternative rather than implying one: uninstall and install the previous MSI, which preserves user data because the installer never created the user-data root, with two honest caveats (CI artifacts expire at 14 days so keeping the old MSI is the user problem, and downgrading across a migration is untested).

NOT CLAIMED, and these are the acceptance remaining clauses verbatim: signature-verified payloads, a pinned allowlisted update endpoint, and a rollback mechanism. All three are downstream of an Authenticode certificate and a decision about where its private key lives. That is LAST_MILE item 6 and an owner decision, and building any of the three before it would mean shipping the unverified updater the acceptance forbids by name.

review.title: A standing check for a test that is skipped in every configuration this repository runs
review.acceptance:
THIS REPOSITORY HAS FOUND THE SAME DEFECT FOUR TIMES AND EACH TIME BY ACCIDENT. A thing exists, it passes, and no gate asks it: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite until PL-0714; components/player/tracks.ts until PW-0306; and the three fail-closed e2e titles until PL-0717, which found them by running two suites to completion and intersecting their skip lists by hand.

REQUIRED: that intersection is computed by a script rather than by somebody remembering to think of it. It reads the JSON reports the e2e job produces for each configuration and reports every test skipped in ALL of them.
REQUIRED: an ALLOWLIST of rows that legitimately run nowhere, declared and reasoned. Today it is exactly two, both media-rig rows, which need hardware no CI runner has. A row that must stay uncovered is a decision somebody records; a row that DRIFTS into being uncovered is a defect, and the allowlist is what distinguishes them.
REQUIRED: the check FAILS the build on an unlisted row. A warning inside a passing pipeline is how all four of the originals survived every gate this repository runs -- validate-workspace-deps.mjs says exactly that about itself and is right.
REQUIRED: non-vacuity. The check must be shown to FAIL against the reports as they were BEFORE PL-0717 -- where the three fail-closed titles were skipped in both configurations -- not merely to pass against today's.
REQUIRED: it runs somewhere a gate asks it, which means `npm run test:scripts` and therefore package.json. A check for things nothing runs that nothing runs would be the joke it sounds like.

OUT OF SCOPE: deciding whether any particular row SHOULD be covered. The check reports and refuses; what to do about a row it names is the owning task's judgement.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 111 by claude-test while implementing PL-0717, whose own notes proposed it. Filed rather than folded in, because PL-0717's surface is .github/workflows/ci.yml alone and this needs a script file plus package.json. BACKLOG rather than READY: it depends on PL-0717, which is what first made a configuration write a JSON report at all, and the check wants one from every configuration.\n\nThe allowedPaths entries are provisional -- the implementer should settle the script's home (scripts/ beside its siblings looks right) and correct them deliberately before starting.

unit.evidence: node --test scripts/assert-no-row-runs-nowhere.test.mjs: 14 tests, 14 pass, 0 fail. NON-VACUITY IS THE CENTRAL CASE AND IT IS DRIVEN TWICE, once on fixtures and once on real reports. (a) The case named "NON-VACUITY: it fails against the reports as they were before PL-0717" builds the two-configuration shape this repository had before PL-0717, with the three fail-closed titles skipped in both, and asserts exit 1 naming all three -- and asserts the two allowlisted media-rig rows are NOT named. A companion case adds the third configuration and the identical reports go green, so the check is not simply hostile to those titles. (b) Against REAL Playwright JSON reports produced locally this round from all three configurations (production+PostgreSQL 51 skipped, development 31 skipped, production-no-database 82 skipped, 153 rows each): three reports gives exit 0, excusing exactly the two media-rig rows; the same two pre-PL-0717 reports alone gives exit 1 naming exactly the three fail-closed titles PL-0717 found by hand. The allowlist is baked into the script with no override flag, so the tests use the real media-rig identities. CI WIRING VERIFIED LOCALLY: PL-0714 mirror-check, extracted from the workflow and run here, reports "test:scripts names 7 suite(s)" and "every suite in the alias has a step in this job"; the workflow still parses (validate 21 steps, e2e-typecheck 4, e2e 14); repo:validate passes. NOT RUN, AND WHY: the test:scripts alias as a whole does not complete -- scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs hangs, which is PL-0735, filed P0 this round after being found by this very command. That hang predates this task, reproduces on a clean worktree of 1474d0b, and is why CI validate has been in progress for over an hour on runs 181 and 182. The six pre-existing suites in the alias are therefore unverified by me today; the one this task adds is verified directly.

review.title: The empty client-key allowlist refusal is asserted by nobody
review.acceptance:
FILED AT gpt-architect's ROUND-112 INVITATION: "If useful, file a narrow follow-up test task for that refusal."

`decidePlaybackTelemetry` has five refusal codes. Four -- session_id_unavailable, session_id_not_transmittable, content_id_not_transmittable and collector_path_not_first_party -- are asserted in player-surface.test.ts, each driven with the viewer ALLOWING diagnostics so that a viewer's yes is shown not to override them. The fifth, client_key_allowlist_empty, is asserted NOWHERE: not in player-surface.test.tsx and not in telemetry-decision.test.ts.

WHY IT WAS NOT COVERED THERE, carried from the round-111 record so this task does not repeat the mistake: it is NOT REACHABLE from `PlaybackTelemetryInput`, which carries enabled, contentId, sessionId, collectorPath, batchSize and intervalSeconds. The allowlist is internal to `playbackTelemetryConfig`. A first draft tried `clientKeys: []`, which is not an input; the object accepted the unknown key silently and the decision stayed enabled. Had that draft's expectation been inverted it would have PASSED while asserting nothing.

REQUIRED: the refusal is driven through whatever surface actually reaches the allowlist, in telemetry-decision.ts's own suite.
REQUIRED: a CONTROL CASE beside it -- the same inputs with a non-empty allowlist producing an enabled decision -- so the refusal is shown to be caused by the allowlist and not by something incidental.
REQUIRED: the refused decision still carries `cmcd: { enabled: false }` as a stated instruction, for the reason the other four do: the controller replays its configuration history and an absent block leaves a previous value in force.
REQUIRED: if the refusal turns out to be unreachable without changing production code, SAY SO AND STOP. gpt-architect's verdict is explicit -- "Do not fabricate coverage for it" -- and an unreachable branch honestly reported is worth more than a test that reaches it by widening an input for the test's benefit.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the allowlist contains or how it is built.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 112 by claude-lead at gpt-architect's explicit invitation in the PL-0724 security verdict. Narrow by design: one test file.

unit.evidence:
THE FIFTH REFUSAL IS NOW REACHED THROUGH REAL PRODUCTION CODE. telemetry-decision.test.ts: 15 passed (was 11); the whole player directory: 23 files, 424 passed; apps/web typecheck clean.

THE SURFACE THAT ACTUALLY REACHES IT, which is the clause the task turned on. client_key_allowlist_empty is decided by CMCD_V2_CLIENT_SAFE_KEYS, which observability COMPUTES at module load from the v2 key registry and which no caller passes. It is therefore not reachable from PlaybackTelemetryInput -- confirmed again here, and the round-111 draft that tried clientKeys: [] is recorded in player-surface.test.tsx rather than deleted. So the seam is the IMPORT: vi.resetModules + vi.doMock over the observability package with importActual spreading every other export, then a dynamic import of telemetry-decision. The real decidePlaybackTelemetry, the real playbackTelemetryConfig and the real guards all run; one derived constant is substituted. NO PRODUCTION CODE WAS CHANGED to make this reachable, which was the task condition -- had reaching it required widening an input for the test, the required answer was to report the branch unreachable and stop.

CONTROL CASE, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The same inputs through the same mocked module graph with a NON-EMPTY allowlist decide ENABLED with cmcd_configured. Without it, refused would be true of a configuration that was already refusing for some unrelated reason -- a guard rejecting these identifiers, the collector path resolving differently through the re-imported graph.

MUTATION-TESTED, AND THE PROBE CAUGHT A WEAK ASSERTION OF MY OWN. With the fail-closed removed from playbackTelemetryConfig (the empty-includeKeys guard made a no-op), the first version of this work had only TWO of three cases go red: the case asserting that the OTHER four reason codes are absent stayed green, because with the decision enabled every not.toContain was still satisfied. An assertion that names only what must be absent passes hardest when nothing is there at all. It now asserts the refusal happened first, and under the same mutant all THREE substantive cases fail. Mutant reverted; telemetry.ts shows no diff.

STATED enabled: false, not an absent block, asserted here for the same reason as the other four: PlaybackController replays its configuration history onto every player it builds, so a decision that said nothing about CMCD would leave a previous value in force -- and on a deployment whose registry derived to nothing, Shaka substitutes allKeysForVersion_(2) for an empty includeKeys, which contains url and nor. An empty allowlist does not send nothing, it sends everything.

ALSO ESTABLISHED, and it corrects a comment rather than a behaviour: telemetry-decision.test.ts header said telemetry.test.ts already pins that an empty allowlist fails closed. It does not. That file asserts the allowlist is NON-empty, which is the opposite case. Until this task nothing anywhere drove the empty one.

review.title: The diagnostics setting is stored, consumed, and reachable by nobody
review.acceptance:
PL-0724 IS DONE AND ITS TITLE IS "The diagnostics switch actually switches diagnostics off". THERE IS NO SWITCH. What exists is the stored per-profile field, `player-surface.tsx` consuming it, and `language-preferences.tsx` round-tripping it WITHOUT EXPOSING IT -- it keeps what it read and sends it back, deliberately, because that form does not own the setting. A viewer cannot set it by any means.

That is not a defect in PL-0724, whose acceptance required the stored field and the player consuming it and which gpt-architect approved on exactly those terms. It is the half nobody owns yet, and `diagnostics-disclosure.tsx` still tells the viewer "This page reports what the product decides; it cannot yet change it" and names PL-0724 as the control that will -- a sentence that is now stale in the way this repository keeps being bitten by.

REQUIRED: the diagnostics section carries a real control that writes the stored field through the existing /api/v1/profiles/preferences endpoint. No second mechanism; PL-0723 established the shape and PL-0724 added the field to it.
REQUIRED: turning it off is PROVEN to persist across a reload against a real production build and a real PostgreSQL, the way PW-0308's language cases are. The reload is the test; everything before it would pass against component state.
REQUIRED: the disclosure text is corrected. It must stop promising a control that now exists, and it must keep reporting the REAL decision from `decidePlaybackTelemetry` rather than describing it -- that property is what PW-0308 was approved for and must not be lost to make room for a toggle.
REQUIRED: the control cannot turn telemetry ON where the decision refuses it. A viewer may decline; a viewer may not override `collector_path_not_first_party` or any other safety refusal. Asserted, because "the toggle wins" is the obvious implementation and PL-0724's acceptance already named it as the wrong one.
REQUIRED: `language-preferences.tsx` keeps round-tripping the field rather than fighting the new control for it -- or the two are reconciled deliberately, with the reason recorded. Two forms writing one field is how a viewer's choice gets silently reverted by saving something unrelated.

OUT OF SCOPE: what CMCD carries, the collector route, and any new telemetry.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 112 by claude-lead while confirming gpt-architect's PW-0308 re-approval clause "diagnostics preference now persists". It does persist, and nobody can choose it. Filed rather than folded into PW-0308 (approved, closing this round) or PL-0724 (approved and closed).

review.title: Corrective: every pwsh step that tolerates a native non-zero exit is broken on the runner
review.acceptance:
WINDOWS #16 (run 37215304869, head 1474d0b) FAILED AT `verifier-negative`, and PW-0602's step-id diagnostics named it: "FIRST FAILING STEP: verifier-negative (failure). Everything after it did not run." Trail: everything before it success, lifecycle=skipped, upload-installers=skipped.

THE STEP CANNOT SUCCEED. It is:

  $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
  node scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs "${env:TEMP}"
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { throw "..." }

Refusing is this step's SUCCESS case, so `node` exits 1 when everything is right. PowerShell 7.4 stabilised `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`, which makes a native non-zero exit a TERMINATING error under `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`. Where it is on, line 2 throws before line 3 runs. The step fails if the verifier refuses (PowerShell throws) and fails if it accepts (the explicit throw fires).

REPRODUCED: the container's pwsh 7.4.6 defaults the preference to False and the step exits 0 -- which is why no local check caught it. Forcing it true gives exactly the runner's failure: 'Program "node" ended with non-zero exit code: 1.'

REQUIRED: the step succeeds when the verifier REFUSES a non-install, and fails when it ACCEPTS one. Both directions, and the second is the one that matters -- this step exists because a verify-install.mjs that returned 0 unconditionally would make every lifecycle PASS meaningless.

REQUIRED: the behaviour does not depend on the runner's default for that preference. A step whose correctness turns on an image's PowerShell configuration is a step that will break again when the image moves, and this project cannot observe that from here.

REQUIRED: the step REPORTS THE EXIT CODE IT SAW, as an annotation. Annotations are the only CI channel this session can read, and the cause above is inferred from a reproduction rather than from the runner's log -- the next run must be able to confirm or refute it without a login.

REQUIRED: no other step is touched, and nothing about what verify-install.mjs checks changes. This is a shell-semantics defect in one step.

FORBIDDEN: deleting the negative check, or softening it to a warning. It is what keeps every positive lifecycle result honest, and its own comment says so.

NOT IN SCOPE: why the lifecycle harness has never run. That is a consequence of this, and whether anything ELSE then fails is the next run's evidence.

=== WIDENED IN ROUND 113, FROM ONE STEP TO THE MECHANISM ===

Windows #17 showed this repair was correct and INCOMPLETE twice over, in two different ways, and both are now in scope.

FIRST, THE SAME STEP. Suppressing the terminating error does not clear the exit code. GitHub runs a shell: pwsh step as pwsh -command ". file; if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath variable:LASTEXITCODE)) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }", so the STEP's exit code is LASTEXITCODE as the body ends -- still 1, from the node whose non-zero exit is this step's success condition. #17 printed this task's own notice and failed anyway. REQUIRED: the step ends with an explicit exit 0 on the success path, and the failure path (verifier wrongly ACCEPTING a non-install directory) still fails.

SECOND, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT STEP. Auditing every shell: pwsh step in windows.yml for the same mechanism -- rather than waiting to be bitten by it again -- found `lifecycle`. It sets ErrorActionPreference = Stop, does NOT suppress the native-exit behaviour, and calls a harness that EXITS NON-ZERO BY DESIGN. So on the runner `& node scripts/windows/lifecycle.mjs` throws at its own line: $code is never captured, the switch that distinguishes exit 1 (a real case failure) from exit 2 (a refusal over arguments or platform) never runs, and the named throw never runs. The step's own comment says collapsing those codes "is how a configuration mistake gets filed as a product defect" -- and on the runner they were collapsed.

THAT HAD NEVER BEEN OBSERVED BECAUSE NO RUN HAS EVER REACHED THAT STEP. Every Windows run in this project's history died at verifier-negative first. The next run is the first to get there, and without this it would have delivered the first lifecycle result the project has ever had with its diagnosis stripped off -- a generic "Program node ended with non-zero exit code: 1" in place of F1-F4 classification.

REQUIRED: all three lifecycle exit codes reach their intended branch and the step's result is right for each -- 0 passes, 1 and 2 fail with the named message.
REQUIRED: the audit is stated as having been performed across every pwsh step in the file, with the steps that are NOT affected named and why, so the next reader does not redo it.
OUT OF SCOPE: ci.yml, whose steps are bash, and whose own hang is PL-0735 and PL-0736.
review.notes:
FILED ROUND 112 by claude-lead from Windows #16's job page. Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 scheme: not a product defect, not a defect in verify-install.mjs, and not caused by PL-0729 -- the verifier exited non-zero against a non-install both before and after that task, correctly.

P0 because it blocks the entire Windows packaging and lifecycle path: lifecycle=skipped and upload-installers=skipped on every run that reaches it, so F1/F2/F3/F4 have never executed and no installer artifact has ever been published.

.github/workflows/windows.yml is reserved by no ACTIVE task (PW-0501, PW-0602, PW-0107 all DONE).

unit.evidence:
TWO SITES OF ONE MECHANISM, BOTH REPRODUCED AND BOTH FIXED, after an audit of every pwsh step in windows.yml rather than a second wait to be bitten.

SITE 1, verifier-negative -- the exit code, not the terminating error. Windows #17 printed this task own notice ("verify-install exited 1 against a directory that is not an install") and failed anyway, which proved execution reached the end of the body. GitHub runs a shell: pwsh step as pwsh -command ". file; if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath variable:LASTEXITCODE)) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }", so the STEP exit code is LASTEXITCODE when the body ends -- still 1 from the node whose non-zero exit is this step success condition. Suppressing a terminating error does not clear an exit code. Fixed with an explicit exit 0.
PROVEN on the real step body, EXTRACTED BY THE YAML PARSER rather than retyped, with only the node call swapped for a controllable exit, through that exact wrapper on pwsh 7.4.6: child exits 1 -> step exit 0 and "correctly refused a non-install directory" printed; child exits 0 (verifier wrongly ACCEPTS) -> step exit 1 and the throw fires. NON-VACUITY: the same harness on the body WITHOUT the new line gives step exit 1 on the first case while printing the success text, which is exactly what #17 did.

SITE 2, lifecycle -- found by the audit, and the more consequential of the two. It sets ErrorActionPreference = Stop, does NOT suppress the native-exit behaviour, and calls a harness that exits non-zero BY DESIGN. On the runner the node call throws at its own line, so $code is never captured, the switch distinguishing exit 1 (a real case failure) from exit 2 (a refusal over arguments or platform) never runs, and the named throw never runs. That step own comment says collapsing those codes "is how a configuration mistake gets filed as a product defect" -- and on the runner they were collapsed.
THIS HAD NEVER BEEN OBSERVED BECAUSE NO RUN HAS EVER REACHED THAT STEP. Every Windows run in this project history died at verifier-negative first. The next one is the first to get there, and without this it would have delivered the first lifecycle result the project has ever had as a generic "Program node ended with non-zero exit code: 1" instead of F1-F4 classification.
PROVEN the same way, on the extracted body with the runner setting forced on: harness exits 0 -> "lifecycle: every automated case passed", step exit 0; exits 1 -> "lifecycle: at least one automated case FAILED -- read the report below", named throw, step exit 1; exits 2 -> "lifecycle: REFUSED to run (arguments or platform). This is a wiring fault in this workflow, not a product failure.", named throw, step exit 1. review.title: CI's validate job no longer finishes: the control-plane suite spends its time in one inner loop
review.acceptance:
CI's `validate` JOB HAS STOPPED FINISHING, AND NOBODY NOTICED BECAUSE A HANG LOOKS LIKE A SLOW RUNNER. CI #181 was still in progress after 1h45m; CI #182 (run 37215304871, head 1474d0b) was still in progress after an hour with e2e and e2e-typecheck both long since SUCCEEDED. Both read from the job page, not the run page.

DIAGNOSED, NOT GUESSED. `node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs` -- a validate-job step -- does not finish in five minutes on a CLEAN CHECKOUT of 1474d0b in a fresh git worktree with no node_modules, which is the CI condition (the suite runs BEFORE `npm ci` in that job). Sampling its children shows each spawned `node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs <command>` taking 10-16 SECONDS. There are 73 scenarios and several commands each.

THE HOT PATH, FROM A --cpu-prof OF ONE `status` INSIDE A FIXTURE REPO (10.1s wall, 9.9s USER -- pure computation, no I/O and no network): `normalizePrefix` at scripts/review-surface.mjs:41 dominates, with its four `.replace()` regexes visible as separate entries, under `dfs` at ai-control-plane.mjs:449.

THE CAUSE IS AN INNER LOOP, and it is three lines. `pathsOverlap(aPaths, bPaths)` calls `normalizePrefix(aRaw)` INSIDE the `bPaths` loop, so a pure function of a small fixed set of declared path strings runs |A|x|B| times per comparison instead of |A|+|B|. `dfs` calls `pathsOverlap` once per (candidate, already-chosen) pair at every node of a search whose budget is 300,000 nodes.

IT IS NOT A CODE REGRESSION. `git log -S` puts both `pathsOverlap` and `const budget = 300000` in f984ab4, the first control-plane commit, unchanged since. What changed is the BOARD: the cost scales with the number of dispatch candidates, and the suite's fixtures are RESET boards where nearly every task is READY. The live repository runs the same command in 0.11s with 137 tasks, because few of them are candidates. Same code, same file size, 100x apart -- the variable is candidate count. The project grew into this.

REQUIRED: the redundant work is removed without changing a single answer. Memoising `normalizePrefix` by its argument takes that one `status` from 10.1s to 2.0s, MEASURED, and `status`, `dispatch` and `ready` produce byte-identical output afterwards except for the generated timestamp -- also measured, by diff. That is the floor, not the target; the remaining 2s is the dfs itself and is worth looking at, but a 5x for a memo on a pure function is the obvious first move.

REQUIRED: the answer is PROVEN unchanged rather than asserted. A performance change to the scheduler that quietly altered a wave would be far worse than the slowness. Diff the output of `status`, `dispatch`, `ready` and `queue` for every agent, before and after, on BOTH the live board and a reset fixture.

MOVED OUT, NOT DROPPED: the `timeout-minutes` clause is now PL-0736. It needs .github/workflows/ci.yml, which PL-0728 holds in REVIEW for the whole of round 112, and the control plane refused this task's claim on exactly that overlap -- the mechanism working. Keeping the two in one task meant NEITHER landed this round, and the half that is startable now is the half that unhangs CI today. PL-0736 carries the clause verbatim and the argument for it, which has not weakened: the performance fix removes today's hang and the timeout removes the class.

REQUIRED: the suite reports progress. 9,570 lines and 73 scenarios print exactly one line, at the end, on success. A suite that says nothing until it is finished cannot be diagnosed when it does not finish -- the scenario that hangs had to be found by sampling child processes from outside. Name each scenario as it starts.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the dfs budget, the wave algorithm, or any scheduling decision. This task makes the same computation cheaper and makes a hang visible. A different wave is a different task and needs a verdict.
review.notes:
FILED BY claude-test DURING PL-0728, round 112, classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme: it is the project's own control-plane tooling and its CI job, not the product.

P0 BECAUSE IT GATES EVERYTHING ELSE. While `validate` cannot finish, no CI run can confirm lint, typecheck, the unit suites, the build, the control-plane suite, the repo validator or the notices suite. Every task closed in rounds 111 and 112 rests on LOCAL evidence plus a green `e2e` job, and that is now a stated fact rather than an assumption. It also means the round-112 directive's instruction to consume CI #182 can be answered only in part, and this is why.

FOUND BY ACCIDENT, AGAIN, AND THE ACCIDENT IS THE POINT. PL-0728 added a suite to `npm run test:scripts`; running the alias to check the addition is what surfaced a hang that two CI runs had already been showing as 'in progress'. The fifth entry in this repository's 'a thing exists and no gate asks it' list is not a test that runs nowhere -- it is a GATE THAT NEVER FINISHES, which is the same failure one level up: a step that neither passes nor fails asserts nothing, and a pipeline waiting on it looks busy rather than broken. That is the argument for the `timeout-minutes` clause being REQUIRED rather than a nicety.

SPLIT ON A REAL REFUSAL, NOT A PREFERENCE. This task was filed holding .github/workflows/ci.yml and `ai:claim` refused it: "PL-0735 paths overlap active task PL-0728 owned by claude-test". PL-0728 is in REVIEW awaiting gpt-architect, so that file is locked for the rest of round 112, and releasing PL-0728 would discard its gate results. The timeout clause left for PL-0736 and this task kept the part that unhangs CI today. Recorded rather than quietly re-scoped, because splitting a P0's acceptance to make it startable is exactly the move that deserves a reviewer's attention.

unit.evidence:
THE SUITE NOW FINISHES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE CLAIM. node scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs: "AI control plane tests passed (73 scenarios) in 137.0s". Before this change the same command did not complete in 20 minutes on this container and had not completed in over an hour on CI runs 181 and 182. npm run test:scripts -- the full alias, seven suites -- now completes in 3m04s with every suite green, including PL-0728 new 14-case suite; that alias had never been observed completing. repo:validate passes and ai-control-plane validate reports 139 tasks, 9 agents.

THE MEASUREMENT, ON THE BOARD THAT ACTUALLY EXERCISES THE PATH. A reset fixture built the way the suite builds one (58 READY candidates, 73 BACKLOG, 8 BLOCKED): one status command took 6.318s BEFORE and 0.168s AFTER, a factor of 38. On the LIVE board the same command is 0.088s before and 0.096s after -- unchanged, because the live board has few simultaneous dispatch candidates and never paid the cost. That asymmetry is the diagnosis restated as a measurement: the cost scales with candidates, not with file size.

THE ANSWER IS PROVEN UNCHANGED, NOT ASSERTED, which matters more than the speed -- a scheduler change that quietly altered a wave would be far worse than the slowness. status, dispatch, ready and queue for all nine agents were captured before and after on BOTH boards: 12 outputs x 2 boards = 24 comparisons, all byte-identical once the generated timestamp line is excluded, 0 real differences. The planner entries were deliberately kept as exactly {task, agent}: a first draft carried the candidate index on the chosen entry and was rewritten to use a shadow array, because a planner returning an extra bookkeeping field is a different return value.

WHAT CHANGED, IN TWO PLACES. (1) normalizePrefix in scripts/review-surface.mjs is memoised by argument -- a pure function over the small fixed set of declared path globs, which pathsOverlap was calling from its INNER loop, so comparing two tasks ran it |A|x|B| times instead of |A|+|B|. (2) planExecutableWave precomputes the pairwise overlap table over its candidates once, instead of recomputing the same pair at every node of a 300,000-node search. Neither changes a decision; both remove repetition of work whose answer cannot change during a plan.

CORROBORATION THAT THE DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT. The instrumented run reports 644 child commands totalling 92.0s. At the 6-10s per command measured before the fix, those same 644 commands are 64 to 107 minutes of child time alone -- which is the hour-plus CI runs 181 and 182 spent showing in progress.

DIAGNOSABILITY, the second half of the task. All 71 numbered scenarios now print their name with elapsed time as they start, so a future hang says where it stopped instead of needing ps from outside -- which is how this one had to be found. Every child command is timed; one over 1s prints a line (nothing did: the slowest was 0.76s, six times under the threshold), and the five slowest print at the end of every run. CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS is tightened from 10 minutes to 2: ten minutes was never reached by this defect, because no individual child was slow enough, and a bound no failure can reach is not a bound.

review.title: The distribution evidence PW-0208 needs is not readable from any CI run
review.acceptance:
PW-0208 HAS BEEN IN REVIEW FOR THREE ROUNDS WAITING FOR EVIDENCE THAT NO CI RUN CAN DELIVER TO A READER HERE. Its nine bullets are about what the installer actually ships. Windows #16 and #17 both built a real MSI and a real NSIS installer, and in both the upload step was skipped behind the verifier-negative failure -- but even a SUCCESSFUL upload would not help: a GitHub artifact needs a login to download, and this session has none. Annotations are the only channel it can read. So the evidence has to be PRINTED by the run, not archived by it.

WHAT THE INVENTORY MUST ESTABLISH, and the three trees must never be conflated -- SOURCE INTENT, PACKAGE BUILD OUTPUT, INSTALLED TREE. This script reports on whichever tree it is pointed at and SAYS WHICH, because evidence from one is not evidence about another.

REQUIRED: every native binary in the tree is enumerated -- .dll, .exe, .so, .dylib, .node -- with size and sha256. A licence argument about binaries begins with knowing which binaries there are.
REQUIRED: libmpv and FFmpeg are reported PRESENT or ABSENT by name, matched on the filenames those projects actually ship (mpv, libmpv, avcodec, avformat, avutil, swresample, swscale, postproc, avfilter, avdevice, ffmpeg, ffprobe), not by a single guessed string. Today the honest answer is ABSENT -- apps/desktop/scripts/notices.mjs says so in its own header and package-sidecar.mjs copies only the Node runtime and the standalone server -- and a check that can only report presence would never notice the day that changes.
REQUIRED: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is reported present, with byte size and the number of components it names. Present-and-empty is the failure PW-0208 already closed one hole against; present-and-stale is the next one.
REQUIRED: the Node runtime's own licence is reported present or absent, because node.exe is shipped and its licence travels with it.
REQUIRED: THE CONTRADICTION CHECK, which is the point of the whole script and the only thing in it that can fail a build. If any libmpv or FFmpeg binary IS present while the notices document still says no shipped component is LGPL, that is a shipped LGPL binary with no written offer and no attribution -- exactly the trap docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found elsewhere ('every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise'). Exit non-zero. The inverse is also a contradiction and also fails: the notices claiming an LGPL component that no binary in the tree corresponds to.
REQUIRED: everything else is REPORTED, not enforced. A script that fails a build over an unexpected DLL would be unusable the first time a legitimate one arrived, and the judgement about what may ship is gpt-architect's and the commander's, not a script's.
REQUIRED: the output is emitted as GitHub ::notice:: lines when running under a runner, so it is readable without a login, AND as plain text otherwise, so it is usable locally. The whole reason this task exists is that evidence nobody can read is not evidence.
REQUIRED: a unit suite over fixture trees, including a tree with an FFmpeg DLL and notices that deny it, shown to FAIL. A contradiction check that has never been seen to fire is a check about nothing.

OUT OF SCOPE, EXPLICITLY: H.264/HEVC patent authorisation. This script reports file names and hashes. It says nothing about whether a decoder may lawfully be distributed, it must not be cited as bearing on that, and it must not cause any decoder to be enabled. That is a commander and counsel decision and no amount of packaging evidence moves it.

OUT OF SCOPE: wiring it into the Windows workflow and into npm run test:scripts. Both files are reserved by tasks in gpt-architect's review queue -- .github/workflows/windows.yml by PL-0733, package.json by PL-0728 -- so that is PL-0738, filed alongside this and blocked on those surfaces. This task delivers the script and its suite; a script nothing runs is this repository's most-repeated defect, and PL-0738 is the entry that keeps it from becoming the sixth instance.
review.notes:
FILED ROUND 113 by claude-lead. The direct cause is the round-113 directive's instruction: 'If Windows #17 does not expose enough artifact evidence, improve the workflow so the NEXT run exposes exactly what gpt-architect needs.' #17 did not, and it would not have even if it had reached its upload step.

THE FINDING THAT SHAPED IT. libmpv and FFmpeg are NOT in the product today. notices.mjs states it in its own header -- 'libmpv and FFmpeg are not in this document because they are not in the product' -- and package-sidecar.mjs copies the Node runtime and the Next standalone server and nothing else. So most of PW-0208's nine bullets are currently questions about a component that does not exist in the build, and the valuable thing is not a one-off answer but a STANDING check that notices the day it does, which is the day the obligations attach.

SURFACE IS DELIBERATELY TWO FILES UNDER scripts/windows/, which nothing active reserves. The precedent for splitting the wiring out is PL-0735/PL-0736 in round 112, where ai:claim refused a P0 on a real overlap and the half that could land did.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/distribution-inventory.test.mjs: 17 tests, 17 pass, 0 fail.

IT FOUND A REAL DEFECT ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN, which is the evidence that matters more than the suite. Pointed at a real packaged sidecar, the script refused: the generated THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md declares three (L)GPL components in its own table -- the two @img/sharp-libvips builds at LGPL-3.0-or-later and @img/sharp-wasm32 -- each with Licence text shipped = **none found**, while the written-offer section of the same document says "No component shipped in this build is LGPL today." Filed as PL-0739. The script was written to catch a hypothetical and caught an actual one.

THE CHECKS, AND WHAT EACH IS WORTH. Everything is REPORTED -- every native binary with size and sha256, libmpv/FFmpeg present or ABSENT by name, the notices file with byte size and component count, the Node runtime and its licence -- because what may ship is a licensing judgement and not a script. Exactly three things REFUSE: an libmpv/FFmpeg binary while the notices deny LGPL; notices claiming a live LGPL component no binary corresponds to; and the document contradicting its own table, which is the one that fired.

THREE TREES NEVER CONFLATED. --kind is required with no default and is printed first: SOURCE INTENT, PACKAGE BUILD OUTPUT, INSTALLED TREE. A test drives all three and another proves the script refuses to run without being told which.

MUTATION-TESTED, BOTH REFUSAL BRANCHES SEPARATELY. Disabling the libmpv/FFmpeg contradiction: cases 4 and 5 go red. Disabling the document-internal contradiction: cases 15 and 17 go red. Both mutants reverted and 17/17 re-run green.

THE CARE THAT MAKES IT REAL RATHER THAN DECORATIVE. FFmpeg does not ship a file called ffmpeg in a library build -- it ships avcodec-61.dll, avformat-61.dll, avutil-59.dll -- and libmpv ships libmpv-2.dll or mpv-2.dll. A check grepping for "ffmpeg" would report ABSENT over a tree full of FFmpeg and pass forever. Eight real filenames are asserted to match and a plausible non-match (helper.node) is asserted not to. Likewise the document check reads TABLE ROWS, not the document, because the written-offer prose says the word LGPL three times by design; a grep would fire every build and be switched off within a week, and there is a test for exactly that.

OUTPUT IS ANNOTATIONS ON A RUNNER AND PLAIN TEXT OTHERWISE, asserted by a test, because the entire reason this task exists is that a GitHub artifact needs a login this session does not have -- evidence nobody can read is not evidence.

NOT CLAIMED: anything about the WINDOWS packaged tree. The real reading was a Linux-built tree, and the script labelled it as such. That gap closes when PL-0738 wires it into the Windows job. H.264/HEVC patent authorisation is addressed by nothing here and the script says so in its own output, with a test that it does.

review.title: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md contradicts itself: the table declares LGPL components the written offer denies
review.acceptance:
MEASURED ON A REAL PACKAGED SIDECAR, NOT REASONED ABOUT. Running apps/desktop/scripts/collect-notices.mjs against the packaged tree produced a document that says, in its own component table:

  | `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64`     | 1.3.2  | LGPL-3.0-or-later                         | **none found** |
  | `@img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64` | 1.3.2  | LGPL-3.0-or-later                         | **none found** |
  | `@img/sharp-wasm32`                | 0.35.3 | Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT  | **none found** |

and then says, forty lines later in the same generated file:

  **No component shipped in this build is LGPL today.** The obligation is stated in advance because the component that will carry it - libmpv, with FFmpeg - is specified and not yet built.

BOTH SENTENCES ARE IN ONE DOCUMENT THE INSTALLER SHIPS. Three LGPL-3.0-or-later components are in the table, their 'Licence text shipped' column says **none found**, and the written offer beneath them denies that any LGPL component exists.

HOW IT HAPPENED, which is the part worth fixing rather than the sentence. The denial is a STATIC STRING in notices.mjs, written when the only LGPL component anyone anticipated was libmpv. It is not derived from the table it sits under, so the table can fill with LGPL rows beneath a sentence swearing there are none -- and it did. sharp arrives as Next's image-optimisation dependency and carries prebuilt libvips, which is LGPL-3.0-or-later. Nobody added it deliberately and nobody noticed.

REQUIRED: the written-offer section is DERIVED FROM THE TABLE, not asserted beside it. If the table has an (L)GPL row the document must say so and the offer must be live; if it has none the document may say none. A generated document must not be able to contradict its own data.
REQUIRED: the three sharp rows are resolved on their merits, and the resolution is a decision somebody records rather than a string edit. Either the LGPL licence text ships (today it is **none found**, which is its own obligation unmet), or sharp is excluded from the packaged sidecar if the product does not use Next image optimisation, or the written offer becomes real for libvips. Three different answers, three different amounts of work, and this task must not pick the cheapest one silently.
REQUIRED: a test that the generator CANNOT emit a denial over a table containing an (L)GPL row. Driven with a fixture that has one, shown to fail before the fix.
REQUIRED: whatever is decided about sharp, the LGPL rows' '**none found**' licence-text column is addressed. Shipping an LGPL binary with neither its licence text nor a working written offer is the concrete obligation, and it is unmet today independently of the contradictory sentence.

NOT IN SCOPE: libmpv and FFmpeg, which remain absent from the product and are PW-0208's subject. This task is about a component that is ALREADY SHIPPING and was not noticed.
NOT IN SCOPE: H.264/HEVC patent authorisation, which no packaging evidence bears on.
review.notes:
FOUND IN ROUND 113 BY POINTING PL-0737's new inventory at a real tree, on its first real run, which is the strongest argument for that task that could exist. It was not found by reading notices.mjs -- that file's own header says 'libmpv and FFmpeg are not in this document because they are not in the product', which is true and was never the problem.

SCOPE CAVEAT, STATED SO THE REVIEWER DOES NOT HAVE TO ASK. The tree measured was built on Linux, so the rows name the linux and linuxmusl sharp variants. A Windows runner installs @img/sharp-libvips-win32-x64, which carries the SAME LGPL-3.0-or-later. Whether the Windows packaged sidecar contains it is not established here and will be, automatically, the first time PL-0738 wires the inventory into the Windows job -- the check is already written and already fires on exactly this shape.

BLOCKED BY SURFACE: apps/desktop/** is reserved by PW-0208, in gpt-architect's review queue. This is material to that review rather than independent of it -- PW-0208 is about shipping an LGPL binary lawfully, and the product is already shipping one.

Gates include rights-review, not just unit, because the decision about sharp is a rights decision and product invariant 6 puts it with the reviewer rather than the implementer.

unit.evidence:
THE CONTRADICTION IS NOT FIXED, IT IS UNREACHABLE. The written offer is now DERIVED from the same sorted entry list the table is rendered from, by copyleftEntries(). A sentence and a table cannot disagree when one is computed from the other, which is what the acceptance asked for: "Prove the document cannot contradict its own table."

node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs: 25 tests, 25 pass (was 22).

THE TEST THAT ASSERTED THE DEFECT IS GONE, AND LOUDLY. The suite contained it("states the written offer, and states that nothing LGPL ships yet") asserting /No component shipped in this build is LGPL today/. It passed every round this generator has existed, because the sentence it pinned was a string rather than a reading of the table -- so that assertion is part of why nobody noticed. This repository standing warning applies to replacing it ("updating an expected value to match reality is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from updating it to match a regression"), so the replacement does NOT pin a new sentence: it asserts the PROPERTY that makes the old one impossible, and drives BOTH branches of the derivation.

FOUR CASES NOW COVER IT. No copyleft row -> the offer says it has nothing to attach to, and the old sentence is asserted ABSENT. A copyleft row -> the offer says live, names the component, and flags that no licence text ships with it. A conjunction (Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT, which is literally @img/sharp-wasm32) counts, because the obligation does -- a matcher that only took a bare LGPL string would have been accurate about two of the three real components, which is harder to spot than being wrong about all three. And a permissive table does NOT trigger it, which is the non-vacuity for the word-boundary matcher.

MUTATION-TESTED, TWO WAYS. Removing the derivation (copyleft = []) reddens 2 cases. Narrowing the matcher to an exact LGPL-3.0-or-later so the conjunction is missed reddens 1. Both reverted, 25/25 green.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL TREE, not a fixture. Regenerating over the actual packaged sidecar now produces: "The offer above is live: 3 component(s) in the table declare a copyleft licence", naming @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64 1.3.2, @img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64 1.3.2 and @img/sharp-wasm32 0.35.3, each marked "no licence text ships with it".

AND IT CAUGHT A BUG IN PL-0737, which is the best evidence either check works. Cross-checking the repaired document through scripts/windows/distribution-inventory.mjs REFUSED IT -- that script "attribution for a component nobody ships" branch asked whether a libmpv or FFmpeg BINARY was present, on the assumption libmpv was the only copyleft component possible. libvips is LGPL, is not libmpv or FFmpeg, and ships as a .node addon. So the first correct document this project has ever generated was refused for telling the truth. The branch now reads the document TABLE instead of the binary list; two cases added there, including non-vacuity that a live offer with nothing in the table to attach to is still refused. That suite is 19/19.

NO LEGAL CONCLUSION DRAWN, which the directive required. docs/LICENSING.md section 7b records the measurement, states that the written offer is now covered and the licence-TEXT obligation is NOT, names three possible resolutions with their differing costs, and explicitly declines to pick one. The scope limits are stated: the tree measured was Linux-built so the rows name linux variants; a Windows runner installs @img/sharp-libvips-win32-x64 with the same licence; whether the WINDOWS packaged sidecar carries it is not established here and will be once PL-0738 wires the inventory into that job. Section 6 patent position is untouched and nothing here bears on it.

recommended.title: test:scripts and the CI validate job can disagree in one direction without anything noticing
recommended.acceptance:
FILED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND REWRITTEN BEFORE ANY WORK. The original said apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs "is run by nothing" and called it the fifth instance of a suite no gate asks. IT RUNS IN CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml, validate job, step id `notices-suite`, `node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs`, added by PL-0714. The claim came from reading that file's own header comment -- "NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY RUNS THIS FILE AUTOMATICALLY YET" -- which was true when PW-0208 wrote it and was made false by PL-0714 a round later. The correction is recorded as a defect.found event.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IT IS SMALLER AND MORE INTERESTING.

1. THE SUITE IS NOT IN `npm run test:scripts`, so it is not in `npm run check` either. It runs on every push and never on a developer's machine through the command this repository tells people to run. That is a coverage asymmetry, not an absence.

2. PL-0714's `mirror-check` CANNOT DETECT THAT, and this is the finding worth the task. It derives the alias's scripts from package.json, derives the job's from the workflow, and fails when a script in the ALIAS has no STEP. The reverse -- a step with no alias entry -- is not checked in either direction. Measured: adding notices.test.mjs to the alias makes the check report "every suite in the alias has a step in this job" and exit 0, and removing it again also exits 0. The mechanism PL-0714 built to end a hand-kept list is itself one-directional, so half the drift it was built for is still invisible.

REQUIRED: `npm run test:scripts` names the suite, so `npm run check` covers it locally.
REQUIRED: the mirror check becomes BIDIRECTIONAL -- a suite step in the validate job with no entry in the alias fails too, with the same kind of message. PL-0714's own words apply: "the note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step did not keep it in step on any of the three occasions", and a one-directional check is half a note.
REQUIRED: both directions are proven to FAIL, by removing an entry from each side in turn and showing the check goes red, not merely by showing it green today.
REQUIRED: the stale header comment in notices.test.mjs is corrected, because it is what produced the false premise above. A comment that outlives the code it describes is the failure this project keeps recording.

OUT OF SCOPE: making apps/desktop an npm workspace. Round 106 measured that and it breaks repo:validate; the account is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.
